mappings.note: Retrieves a stated detail about the landlord's son; identifying details/characters in the text, not LO-2's open response.
Recall of what the character believed - a stated detail. Rejected LO-2, which is for questions needing inference beyond the line.
Who-question on a plot fact. LO-1 covers identifying characters and details; no inference asked, so not LO-2.
Vocabulary item: names the word for 'a liquid with magical effects'. Word meaning from context, so C-ENG3.2-LO-1 rather than the comprehension LO C-ENG2.1-LO-1.
Three-mark 'how did the sage help' needs the pupil to assemble the sage's motive and instructions in writing; LO-2's written response, not LO-1's single detail.
Stated detail (the potion). LO-1; rejected C-ENG3.2-LO-1 because no word meaning is being deduced.
Characterisation MCQ on the sage. LO-1 explicitly covers identifying characters; rejected C-ENG3.2-LO-1 as the options are traits, not glossed vocabulary.
Prediction with a reason - reading beyond the text and justifying in writing. LO-2, not LO-1, which stops at what is on the page.
Names the sage. Pure detail retrieval; LO-2 rejected as nothing is inferred.
Characterisation MCQ on Rama Natha at the story's opening; identifying characters is LO-1's wording.
'Why was he angry' requires linking the copper vessel to the failed potion; a written inferential response, so LO-2 over LO-1.
Quantity stated in the text (five litres). LO-1 detail retrieval; no inference, so not LO-2.
Characterisation MCQ on Madhumati. LO-1; rejected LO-2 because the trait is directly evidenced.
Asks the pupil to trace the sequence of events by which the wealth was built - LO-1 names 'the sequence of ideas and events'.
Single stated fact (bananas). LO-1; LO-2 rejected as no reasoning is required.
Asks why the sage chose a trick over plain truth - the distractors are all plausible, so the pupil must read between the lines. LO-2, not LO-1.
Recounts the sage's instructions in order; the sequence-of-events half of LO-1, not an inference.
Madhumati's worry is not stated as a cause; the pupil must infer it from his neglect. LO-2 over LO-1.
True/false check against a stated attitude. Detail verification, so LO-1 rather than LO-2.
The sage's reason for insisting on personal labour is implicit; inferential written answer, so LO-2.
Recall of the instruction about the dew. LO-1; rejected LO-2 as it needs no reading between the lines.
True/false on the sage's unstated intent - a judgement about motive, which is LO-2 territory, not LO-1 detail-checking.
Requires combining the winter-only dew with the six-year span to explain the plantation; inference, so LO-2.
Character's stated reaction to the failed dew. LO-1; LO-2 rejected because the feeling is on the page.
True/false characterisation. LO-1 covers identifying characters; no extended reasoning as LO-2 would want.

Five-mark answer: the comprehension load is LO-2's written response, and the length demands the coherent beginning-middle-end of C-ENG4.1-LO-2. Rejected LO-1 as far too small a claim for a 5-mark item.
The sage's final revelation is stated at the close; detail/sequence retrieval, so LO-1.
True/false against an event that never happens in the text - checking details, so LO-1 not LO-2.
Duration stated (six years). LO-1 detail retrieval.
True/false on an invented journey to the Himalayas; detail verification, LO-1.
Links belief to action across the story - a written analytical response. LO-2, not LO-1's single detail.
True/false on Madhumati's stated help with the plants. LO-1.
'Explain the process' is the sequence of events restated in order - the explicit wording of LO-1 - rather than an inference for LO-2.
What the father left him: stated detail. LO-1.
The gold coins' significance is symbolic and never stated; going beyond the text, so LO-2 over LO-1.
Causal 'why' answered by joining his obsession to his neglect; inferential, so LO-2.
Asks how the sage's storytelling worked as teaching - a judgement about narrative technique, LO-2's critical response, not LO-1.
Why others could cheat him must be inferred from his credulity. LO-2 over LO-1.
What the couple did after the revelation is narrated at the end; sequence of events, LO-1.
Causal 'why was Madhumati worried' - inference about an unstated fear. LO-2.
Five-mark character-arc analysis: LO-2 for the critical reading, C-ENG4.1-LO-2 for the sustained coherent piece it must be written as. Rejected LO-1, which does not reach analysis.
What he asked the sage about: stated detail. LO-1.
'Discuss the role and influence' of a character is an evaluative written response; LO-2, not LO-1's naming of characters.
What he did next - sequence of events. LO-1.
Five-mark 'evaluate... why or why not' takes a position and sustains it: LO-2 for the critical judgement, C-ENG4.1-LO-2 for the coherent extended answer.
Names the character who reveals the truth. LO-1 detail/character retrieval.
Theme question - LO-1's 'identify main ideas' is the tighter claim than LO-2, which is for open-ended questioning.
Causal 'why' needing his belief joined to his neglect; inferential, so LO-2 rather than LO-1.

Asks the pupil to invent a new ending: C-ENG3.2-LO-2 names narrating imaginary situations, and C-ENG4.1-LO-1 the drafting of it from the story's clues. Rejected C-ENG2.1-LO-2, as nothing here is comprehension of the given text.
Recounts the character's stated reaction. LO-1; LO-2 rejected as the reaction is on the page.
Draws the life lesson and applies it to the pupil - LO-1 ends with 'relate them to personal experience', which LO-2 does not.
Describes the character before the turning point; identifying characters, LO-1.
Setting-to-message analysis is never stated in the text; LO-2's critical written response over LO-1.
Traces how the wife's selling built the wealth - sequence of events, LO-1.
'In what ways does the sage represent wisdom' asks for inference from his conduct; LO-2, not LO-1's identification.
Two-part item ending in 'what moral do we derive' - main idea plus character change, both LO-1. Rejected LO-2 as the moral is the text's own point.
The role of time in the transformation is an interpretive claim; LO-2 over LO-1.
Contrasts two characters on evidence given in the text; identifying characters, LO-1.
'Reflect on the theme of self-deception' - reading between the lines, LO-2 rather than LO-1's stated main idea.
Describes the character with examples from the story; evidence is on the page, so LO-1 not LO-2.
